note.text:
Burning (combustion) is a reaction of a substance with oxygen that gives out heat and light.
Three things are needed for a fire (the fire triangle): fuel, oxygen (air) and heat (to reach the ignition temperature). Remove any one and the fire goes out.
Paper is made of cellulose, which contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. When it burns: paper + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (+ ash).
Cooking gas (butane, propane) and methane burn with a blue flame when there is enough air:
methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water
With too little air the flame is yellow and smoky, and poisonous carbon monoxide and soot (carbon) form. Always cook in a well-aired room.

vars.x: a lid is put on a pan of burning oil

worked_example.problem: Why does the fire go out when {x}?
steps: A fire needs fuel, oxygen and heat.
The lid stops oxygen from reaching the oil.
worked_example.answer: The oxygen is removed, so the fire triangle is broken.

cards.idea: A fire needs fuel, oxygen and heat. Taking away any one puts the fire out.
example: Water cools a wood fire (removes heat).
Sand on a fire cuts off oxygen.

cards.idea: Paper and cooking gas contain carbon and hydrogen; they burn to carbon dioxide and water.
With too little air a flame is yellow and smoky, and poisonous carbon monoxide forms.
example: A blue gas flame has enough air.
Never burn charcoal in a closed room.

pick.q: A gas cooker burns with a yellow, smoky flame. What does this show?
e: Plenty of air gives a blue flame.
pick.y: Too little air gives a yellow, sooty flame.

pick.q: Why is it dangerous to burn charcoal in a closed room?
pick.y: With little air, carbon monoxide forms; it can kill.

pick.q: Which three things are needed for burning?
e: Nitrogen does not support burning; heat is needed.

pick.q: Sand is thrown on a small fire. Which side of the fire triangle is removed?
e: The fuel is still there under the sand.
Sand mainly cuts off the air.
Nitrogen is not part of the triangle.
pick.y: Sand stops air reaching the fuel.

pick.q: Water is poured on a burning log. How does this put out the fire?
pick.r: It cools the fuel below its ignition temperature.

pick.q: What are the products when cooking gas burns in plenty of air?
e: Carbon is only formed with too little air.
pick.y: Fuels with carbon and hydrogen give carbon dioxide and water.

pick.q: Which elements does paper mainly contain?
e: Paper is not a metal compound.
pick.y: Paper is cellulose: C, H and O.

pick.q: A gas cooker burns with a yellow, smoky flame. What does this show?
e: Plenty of air gives a blue flame.
pick.y: Too little air gives a yellow, sooty flame.

pick.q: Why is it dangerous to burn charcoal in a closed room?
pick.y: With little air, carbon monoxide forms; it can kill.

right.text: Burning gives out heat and light.
A blue flame shows there is enough air.
Cooking gas burns to carbon dioxide and water.
Removing the fuel stops a fire.

wrong.text: A fire can burn without oxygen if it is hot enough.
Water on a fire adds oxygen and makes it burn faster.
wrong.explain: Water cools the fire and puts it out.

wrong.text: A yellow smoky flame burns more cleanly than a blue one.
wrong.explain: The yellow flame has soot and carbon monoxide.
